title: Everything we know about the Louvre jewellery heist
facts: Thieves wielding power tools broke into the Louvre Museum in Paris in broad daylight and escaped with eight items of jewellery. [cite: 411]
Four suspects used a vehicle-mounted mechanical lift to access the Galerie d'Apollon via a balcony near the River Seine. [cite: 414]
Two of the thieves entered the Louvre Museum by cutting through a first-floor window using power tools. [cite: 415, 416]
The thieves cut through the glass of two display cases inside the Louvre Museum to access the jewels. [cite: 417]
The thieves remained inside the Louvre Museum for four minutes before escaping on two waiting scooters at 09:38. [cite: 419]
A preliminary report indicated that one in three rooms in the raided area of the Louvre Museum lacked CCTV cameras. [cite: 418]
The French culture ministry stated that the Louvre museum's wider alarms did sound during the burglary. [cite: 423]
A museum staff-member prevented the thieves from setting fire to their vehicle outside the Louvre Museum. [cite: 424]
Approximately 60 investigators are working on the case regarding the theft at the Louvre Museum. [cite: 427]
The stolen items from the Louvre Museum include 19th-century diadems, necklaces, ear-rings, and brooches that once belonged to French royalty or imperial rulers. [cite: 430, 431]
Empress Eugénie's crown was found damaged on the escape route after apparently being dropped by the thieves. [cite: 433]
Officials at the Louvre requested help from the French government earlier in the year to restore the museum's ageing exhibition halls. [cite: 439]
French President Emmanuel Macron previously pledged to redesign the Louvre Museum as part of the New Renaissance project costing between 700 million and 800 million euros. [cite: 440]
Thieves broke into the Adrien Dubouche Museum in Limoges last month and stole porcelain works reputedly worth 9.5 million euros. [cite: 452]
Armed robbers raided the Hieron Museum in Burgundy in November 2024 and stole 20th-century artworks. [cite: 454]
